title: Behold What Wondrous Grace
description: Behold What Wondrous Grace in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 64, headed “Adoption, 1 John 3. 1 &c. Gal. 4. 6”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold what won-drous grace The Fa-ther hath be-stow'd On sin-ners of a mor-tal race, To call them sons of God!

lines: On sinners of a mortal race,
To call them sons of God!
The Jewish world knew not their King,
How great we must be made;
But when we see our Saviour here,
We shall be like our head.
May purge our souls from sense and sin,
As Christ the Lord is pure.
Send down thy Spirit like a dove
My faith shall Abba, Father, cry,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
